summary: Confirmed DONE by 60633eff3 (#710), which is also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. The desktop-only empty registry and the Effect.sleep(100ms) reconcile are gone. Every mode now reads settings once, derives the configured identities without building drivers (listConfigured), and reads <providerStatusCacheDir>/<instanceId>.json for each one in parallel during the ProviderRegistry layer build. The validated snapshots go into providersRef before the HTTP listener exists, so the first server-config snapshot carries the last-known providers and models. When a driver arrives after the boot gate opens, its cached entry is either adopted (fingerprint match) or kept until a demand probe replaces it. It is never overwritten by a placeholder, because makeManagedServerProvider never probes or publishes on construction. I could not find another composition, caller or mode with the old gap.

evidence.note: Registry starts empty in every mode (no config.mode branch remains). Settings are read once, the map comes from deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap, and identities come from resolveConfiguredProviderIdentities (schema decode only, no driver.create).

plannedIdentities is exposed as listConfigured (230). Drivers are built only after gateReleased (187-208). getInstance forces the build on demand for configured ids (218-227). The old DesktopSettingsReconcileLive with Effect.sleep("100 millis") at f1be4abc7 was removed.

resolveConfiguredProviderIdentities and resolveInstanceEnabled use the same decode and enabled derivation as buildEntry (266-275), so the seeded identity's enabled flag matches what the driver later reports.

Boot reads listConfigured and reads one cache file per identity in parallel inside the provider.status-cache.seed phase. Identity is validated by hydrateCachedProviderFromConfig, and mismatches are logged and dropped.
Persisted snapshots are upserted into providersRef at layer build with publish:false and persist:false, before any driver exists.
settleBootArrival either adopts the persisted snapshot (matching fingerprint) or keeps the cached entry. The driver's placeholder is upserted only when providersRef has no entry for the instance.

Instances still awaiting driver arrival stay in knownInstanceIds, so the prune at 892-902 does not drop cached entries while drivers build. Instances removed from settings before they arrived are dropped.

Construction never probes and never publishes the initial placeholder to streamChanges, so a kept cached entry is not replaced by 'Checking...' when the driver's change subscription starts (ProviderRegistry.ts:816-821).
Validates instanceId, driver and enabled against the settings-derived identity, and takes displayName and accentColor from current settings.
The only composition of ProviderRegistryLive and ProviderInstanceRegistryHydrationLive, shared by desktop, web and headless.
markHttpServing (called from server.ts:723 after HttpRouter.serve) releases the boot gate, so driver construction is off the listener critical path.
loadServerConfig reads providerRegistry.getProviders, which now returns the seeded list. The auditor's 1160 is loadDiagnosticsSnapshot.
revalidateStale is forked only after the snapshot is emitted. If a client asked before the drivers arrived, a pass reruns on boot arrival (ProviderRegistry.ts:866-868).
With the real hydration layer, listConfigured is populated from settings and listInstances stays empty until the gate opens.
Covers serving the persisted snapshot before the driver exists, adoption on fingerprint match, keeping a stale snapshot until a demand probe, and the placeholder when nothing was persisted.

fixDefects: None found. Minor non-defects: (1) No single test drives the real ProviderInstanceRegistryHydrationLive plus an on-disk cache file through to getProviders before the gate opens. Each half is tested separately (ProviderRegistry.test.ts:1601 and the fake-registry tests at 3098+). (2) A seeded snapshot that was not adopted can show cached usage limits (rateLimits carry no timestamp) until the demand pass probes it. That pass has concurrency 2 and a 250 ms stagger, so with many providers the window is a few seconds. This is an accepted last-known-state tradeoff. (3) The enabled-mismatch rejection at providerStatusCache.ts:62 falls back to the placeholder after an offline toggle, as the auditor noted. This is deliberate.
decisionReason: Nothing remains. The fix is merged and covers every mode.
correction: Small citation fix only: the server-config snapshot reads getProviders in loadServerConfig at apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:1175. Line 1160 is loadDiagnosticsSnapshot. The classification stands.
